section_summary: This section covers U.S. State Department and SCAP records from August through December 1949 regarding Japanese industrial monopolies, cartels, and zaibatsu deconcentration under the Allied Occupation. Key issues include intense public and official debate over Prime Minister Shigeru Yoshida's plan to privatize the state tobacco monopoly, as well as an extensive report by SCAP Antitrust Chief Edward C. Welsh and State Department commentary evaluating progress and policy on business democratization. Additionally, the records document multiple SCAP directives (SCAPINs 2045, 2057, 2058, and 2065) releasing and removing dozens of reorganized Japanese companies from restricted listings, alongside related diplomatic correspondence and intelligence notes.

subfiles.about: Transmits Japanese newspaper editorials analyzing Premier Yoshida's proposal to transfer the government tobacco monopoly to private management.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Enclosures to Despatch 612 provide translations of editorials from Shin Tokyo and Asahi Shimbun analyzing Premier Yoshida's plan to privatize tobacco manufacturing. Both editorials urge caution due to government revenue needs and risks of foreign cartel dominance.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 612: Discussions between China-American Leaf Tobacco and the Japan Monopoly Public Corporation

subfiles.about: Action copy cover sheet for Foreign Service Despatch No. 651 transmitting SCAPIN 2045.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Foreign Service cover sheet transmitting SCAPIN 2045 regarding company removals from the restricted concerns schedule.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 651 Cover Sheet: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Directs the Japanese Government to remove 67 specified companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP memorandum ordering the removal of 67 designated companies and subsidiaries across textiles, mining, shipping, and chemicals from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2045: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Reports on political opposition in Japan to privatizing the tobacco monopoly and transmits an editorial from the Nippon Times.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Reports on growing political opposition to privatizing the tobacco monopoly, notes authorization for Eric Baruch to import leaf tobacco experimentally, and encloses a critical Nippon Times editorial.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 776: Status of Proposal to Turn Over Japanese Tobacco Monopoly to Private Management

subfiles.about: Requests a copy of an official U.S. policy statement pledging to prevent revival of trade cartels in Japan and Western Germany.
subfiles.summary: Letter requesting a copy of an official U.S. policy declaration regarding prevention of trade cartels in Japan and Germany.
subfiles.title: Request for Policy Statement on Revival of Trade Cartels
subfiles.to: Far Eastern Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: Transmits Edward C. Welsh's report and David Maynard's memorandum on the business democratization program to W. Walton Butterworth.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum forwarding Welsh's report on business democratization and Maynard's critique to Butterworth, noting ITP's interest in hiring Welsh.
subfiles.title: Transmittal of Report on Democratization of Business Program in Japan

subfiles.about: Provides critical analysis and recommendations on Edward Welsh's report regarding the business democratization program in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Disagrees with Welsh's premise of indefinite occupation to enforce democratization, recommending cutting the Anti-Trust and Cartel Division to two or three advisors by July 1950.
subfiles.title: Comments on Report on Democratization of Business Program

subfiles.about: Provides filing instructions and context for Edward C. Welsh's report prepared for Under Secretary Voorhees.
subfiles.summary: File note stating Welsh's report was prepared for Voorhees and reflects personal views, not official GHQ SCAP policy.
subfiles.title: File Note on Report Prepared for Under Secretary Voorhees

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report surveying the accomplishments, challenges, and future requirements of SCAP's business democratization and anti-monopoly programs in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Welsh details major achievements in dissolving zaibatsu holding companies, distributing securities, breaking up excessive economic concentrations, and establishing fair trade laws. He warns that Japanese leaders lack democratic experience and strongly cautions against premature transfer of authority, arguing that relaxing SCAP vigilance will resurrect monopolies and cartels.
subfiles.title: Report on Democratization of Business Program

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of SCAPIN 2057 and SCAPIN 2058 to the Department of State.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding copies of SCAPIN 2057 and SCAPIN 2058 releasing companies from limitations and removing them from restricted listings.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 854: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns, and Release of Certain Companies from Limitation of Activities and Report Requirements

subfiles.about: Releases 55 specified Japanese concerns from activity limitations and reporting requirements.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP memorandum releasing 55 designated industrial, textile, chemical, and regional companies from activity limitations and reporting requirements established under earlier directives.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2057: Release of Certain Companies from Limitation of Activities and Report Requirements

subfiles.about: Removes 62 designated Japanese companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP memorandum ordering the removal of 62 specified companies across manufacturing, shipping, textiles, and chemicals from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2058: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns

subfiles.about: Routes Donald Silverman's inquiry regarding Japanese cartels and trade policy to USPOLAD in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Department of State Form DS-9 routing slip transmitting Donald Silverman's research inquiry to USPOLAD for appropriate response.
subfiles.title: Department of State Transmittal Slip to USPOLAD

subfiles.about: Inquires about information and materials regarding international trade policy and cartel problems in Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: Student researcher letter requesting available information and materials on Japanese industry, trade policy, and cartel problems.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Japanese Industry and Cartel Problems

subfiles.about: Reports confidential advice from Admiral Decker that a Navy External Security Detachment from China and Taiwan was transferred to Yokosuka.
subfiles.summary: Confidential memorandum reporting Admiral Decker's disclosure that a Navy External Security Detachment was relocated from China and Taiwan to Yokosuka without mission directives.
subfiles.title: Establishment of External Security Detachment in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits a GHQ SCAP press release announcing the removal of 62 concerns from restricted listings under SCAPIN 2058.
subfiles.summary: Incoming airgram transmitting a SCAP press release detailing the criteria and company categories for removing 62 concerns from restricted listings.
subfiles.title: SCAP Press Release on Removal of 62 Concerns from Restricted Listing

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of SCAPIN 2065 removing 26 companies from the schedule of restricted concerns.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch forwarding copies of SCAPIN 2065 releasing 26 companies from the schedule of restricted concerns.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 905: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Firms

subfiles.about: Removes 26 designated companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.from: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: SCAP memorandum removing 26 specified companies across railways, heavy machinery, chemicals, and shipping from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 2065: Removal of Certain Companies from the Schedule of Restricted Concerns
